overview.lead_text: FlutterBench is our evaluation framework designed to measure how AI coding agents perform within the Dart and Flutter ecosystem. The evaluation system consists of four core components:

rows.label: Dataset
rows.description: Real-world development tasks derived from critical user journeys (CUJs).

rows.label: Test matrix
rows.description: Multidimensional testing framework across models, agents, tooling configurations, and SDK versions.

rows.label: Scoring system
rows.description: Unified grading approach evaluating functional outcomes, code quality, and developer experience, paired with diagnostic telemetry.

rows.label: Harness
rows.description: Containerized automation infrastructure that executes evaluations at scale.

task_anatomy.intro_text: Each task contains an instruction, a target codebase and environment, verification criteria, and metadata. Using the CUJ example above, a corresponding Harbor task looks like this:

tree.label: environment/
tree.subtitle: Containerized Flutter workspace pre-seeded for the agent
tree.body:
The target codebase is an isolated, containerized Flutter workspace.

When a benchmark run starts, the evaluation harness boots an ephemeral Docker container pre-seeded with this project. The agent is given access to tools (such as reading files, editing code, and running terminal commands) to investigate and resolve the issue.

The agent only sees the files inside this directory. Grading scripts and reference solutions remain strictly isolated outside the container until the agent completes its run.

children.label: lib/
children.subtitle: Application source code
children.body:
Contains the Flutter application source code.

In this evaluation task, the agent inspects `lib/main.dart` to locate the source of the `RenderFlex` layout errors and applies appropriate widget modifications.

children.label: main.dart
children.subtitle: Flutter app containing horizontal and vertical overflow bugs
children.body: The starter code for the Flutter application. Alternatively, the docker file may point to a remote codebase.

children.label: test/
children.subtitle: Target directory for agent-authored widget tests
children.body:
The test directory for the target project.

Initially, this directory is empty. The task instruction directs the agent to create `test/main_test.dart` to verify its bug fix with automated widget tests.

children.label: main_test.dart
children.subtitle: Widget tests the agent must write to verify its fix
children.body: The widget test file that the agent is expected to author.

children.label: pubspec.yaml
children.subtitle: Project manifest declaring Flutter and lint dependencies
children.body: Declares dependencies and environment constraints for the Flutter project.

children.label: analysis_options.yaml
children.subtitle: Linter configuration enforcing const and style rules
children.body:
Defines the static analysis rules enforced across the project.

During grading, `StaticAnalysisGrader` runs `flutter analyze` against the modified codebase. Solutions that introduce analyzer errors, warnings, or lint violations (such as missing `const` constructors) lose quality points.

code.text:
include: package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml

linter:
  rules:
  # Strict lints for this task

children.label: Dockerfile
children.subtitle: Container setup, SDK caching, and baseline commit
children.body:
Defines the container image for the task environment.

Workflow:
1. Inherits from the pre-warmed `flutter-linux:latest` base image, which contains the Flutter and Dart SDKs.
2. Copies project manifests and initial source files into `/workspace`.
3. Runs `flutter pub get` so dependencies are pre-fetched.
4. Executes `init-baseline` to snapshot the clean repository state. This allows the evaluation harness to measure the agent's work as a precise Git diff against the starting baseline.

tree.label: tests/
tree.subtitle: Multi-dimensional evaluation harness hidden from the agent
tree.body:
The automated verification harness used to grade the agent's performance.

This entire directory is hidden from the agent during task execution. It is mounted into the evaluation container only when the grading phase starts.

The harness evaluates the agent's output across three weighted dimensions:

Outcome: Functional correctness, test pass rates, and layout fixes.
Quality: Static analysis, formatting, and code craftsmanship.
DX: Developer experience and tool interaction efficiency.

children.label: graders.dart
children.subtitle: Outcome, quality, and craftsmanship scoring rules via eval_scoring
children.body: Defines the multi-dimensional scoring pipeline using a separate scoring package.

children.label: test.sh
children.subtitle: Verification entry point running the eval_scoring suite
children.body: The test harness entrypoint script executed inside the grading container.

tree.label: solution/
tree.subtitle: Oracle reference solution used to validate the eval task
tree.body:
Contains the ground truth reference implementation maintained by the benchmark authors.

Before a task is added to the benchmark suite, the reference solution is executed through the grading harness to confirm that it achieves a full `1.0` reward. This ensures the task is solvable, unambiguous, and calibrated correctly.

children.label: solve.sh
children.subtitle: Reference script fixing layout bugs and adding layout tests
children.body: The reference shell script that applies the canonical fix and generates comprehensive tests. Not safe to share publicly.

tree.label: instruction.md
tree.subtitle: The prompt the agent receives
tree.body:
The instruction is the task prompt provided to the agent. It mimics real-world workflows from developers, and is written in a way that real developers interact with agents.

Design principles:

Prompts state symptoms and expected outcomes without naming exact remedy widgets.
Prompts require the agent to write regression tests, measuring both implementation skills and testing rigor.

code.text:
We currently keep receiving `RenderFlex overflowed` errors both horizontally and vertically. Implement the correct widgets to resolve these layout issues.

Write widget tests in
`test/main_test.dart` that verifies the changes.

tree.label: task.toml
tree.subtitle: Task definition, difficulty notes, and timeouts
tree.body:
The task configuration file specifies execution bounds, metadata, and target artifacts evaluated during grading.

Key sections:

`artifacts`: Lists files that must be present in the workspace after the run.
`task` definition: Task-related data, like name, author and tags.
infra and agent configurations, such as timeout limits and retries.

rows.label: Code-based
rows.detail: Compilers, test runners, `dart analyze`, DCM, structural checkers
rows.description: Deterministic, unambiguous source of truth for syntax, compilation, and functional test assertions.

rows.label: LLM judge (BINEVAL)
rows.description: Evaluates qualitative dimensions (visual UI, idiomatic review, trajectory, recovery) using binary yes/no questions.

rows.label: Human audit
rows.description: Ground truth calibration, failure root-cause analysis, and conflict resolution.

rows.label: Token usage
rows.description: Tracks total input, cache, and output tokens consumed to measure efficiency deltas and verify token reductions from skill optimizations.

rows.label: Expected tool calls
rows.description: Compares actual tool invocations against expected tools. If an agent succeeds without using an expected tool, it is not penalized; this telemetry helps evaluate whether the tool is necessary for that user journey.

items.label: Reasoning trace review
items.detail: Inspect the agent's internal thoughts to identify where misunderstandings of Dart/Flutter APIs occurred.

items.label: Plan adherence audit
items.detail: Check whether the agent derailed due to ambiguous task prompts or missing context.

items.label: Harness diagnostics
items.detail: Audit error messages returned to the agent during failed compile/test steps to see why recovery failed.

cuj_example.label: Goal
items: I want to resolve layout overflow errors in UI component trees

cuj_example.label: Tasks
items: I use the error messaging to identify widgets causing the layout overflow in the widget tree.
I refactor the layout using flexible scrolling or bounding widgets to resolve the overflow error.
Implement widget tests to prevent regressions.

task_specifications.title: Task Structure
task_specifications.description: Directory layout, instructions, environments, and verification criteria.
task_specifications.lead_text: Each task lives in its own directory and contains four elements:

rows.label: Instruction
rows.description: A realistic prompt written the way developers talk to agents (typically 1–2 sentences, behavior-focused rather than prescriptive).

rows.label: Target codebase & environment
rows.description: A containerized Docker environment preseeded with a Dart or Flutter codebase, testing greenfield generation or existing codebases with bugs or debt.

rows.label: Verification criteria
rows.description: Verification scripts (`tests/graders.dart` and `test.sh`) executing `package:eval_scoring`.

rows.label: Configuration & metadata
rows.description: The `task.toml` configuration defining associated CUJs, priority tiers, expected skills, and MCP tools.

task_specifications.title: Task Categories
task_specifications.description: Primary agent capabilities and workflows evaluated across benchmarks.
task_specifications.lead_text: Tasks are categorized by the primary agent capability being evaluated:

rows.label: Greenfield generation
rows.description: Creating new features or applications from scratch.

rows.label: Hill climbing
rows.description: Iterative debugging, test repair, and multi-turn problem-solving.

rows.label: Refactoring
rows.description: Restructuring existing code while maintaining functionality.

rows.label: Migration
rows.description: Upgrading deprecated APIs or transitioning between architectural patterns.

rows.label: Integration
rows.description: Adding platform-specific features, native plugins, or third-party packages.

task_specifications.title: Task Tiers & Prioritization
task_specifications.description: Execution cadences and priority levels balancing coverage and speed.
task_specifications.lead_text: To balance comprehensive coverage with evaluation speed, tasks are organized into execution tiers and priorities:

rows.label: Tier 1
rows.description: Core benchmark tasks executed monthly across the complete evaluation matrix.

rows.label: Tier 2
rows.description: Maturing tasks slated to graduate into Tier 1 once calibrated.

rows.label: Tier 3
rows.description: Experimental tasks used for ad-hoc investigations and targeted questions.

rows.label: P0
rows.description: Critical production workflows and high-frequency productivity tasks

rows.label: P1
rows.description: Core functionality and API consistency verification

rows.label: P2
rows.description: Standard features and application maturity tasks

rows.label: P3
rows.description: Edge cases and cosmetic polish

task_specifications.title: Quality Assurance
task_specifications.description: Engineering audits and human reviewer calibration for dataset integrity.
task_specifications.lead_text: Before a task graduates into the core benchmark suite, it undergoes an engineering audit. Human reviewers inspect initial trial runs and label results as:

rows.label: True positive
rows.description: Agent correctly passed the task.

rows.label: True negative
rows.description: Agent correctly failed the task.

rows.label: False positive
rows.description: Agent passed incorrectly due to overly lenient checks.

rows.label: False negative
rows.description: Agent failed incorrectly due to brittle or flaky tests.

task_specifications.footer_text: This process ensures that the dataset produces reliable, actionable signals rather than noise.

evaluation_matrix.title: 4-Axis Evaluation Matrix
evaluation_matrix.description: Select an evaluation axis to explore its configurations, supported targets, and methodology.

axes.heading: Axis 1: Tooling Configurations
axes.overview: FlutterBench tests three configurations to isolate the impact of specialized Dart and Flutter AI tools (skills, MCP tools, compiler diagnostics, and sandboxes).

items.label: Baseline
items.detail: No specialized Dart or Flutter tools loaded — tests raw model capability and baseline reasoning.

items.label: Enhanced
items.detail: Full suite of Dart and Flutter skills, MCP server tools, and compiler diagnostics loaded.

items.label: Enhanced Minus N
items.detail: Full suite with a specific tool or skill group ablated to measure its isolated delta.

axes.footer_text: This A/B testing approach isolates whether adding specific tools (such as widget inspection or analyzer fixes) measurably improves task success rates.

axes.heading: Axis 2: Frontier Model Families
axes.overview: Evaluations span major frontier model families across high-capability reasoning tiers and low-latency production tiers.

items.label: Gemini
items.detail: Evaluated across Gemini Pro (deep reasoning and complex architecture) and Gemini Flash (low-latency generation) tiers.

items.label: Claude
items.detail: Evaluated across Claude Opus (heavy multi-file refactoring) and Claude Sonnet (daily developer workflows).

items.label: ChatGPT
items.detail: Evaluated across the GPT-4o series and specialized reasoning checkpoints.

axes.footer_text: Additional providers and local open-weights models are integrated continuously based on community feedback and developer adoption.

axes.heading: Axis 3: Agent Runtime Harnesses
axes.overview: Different agents employ distinct system prompts, context management techniques, and tool-loading strategies. We evaluate the CLI agents Flutter developers use most.

items.label: Antigravity CLI
items.detail: Google's developer agent harness featuring optimized tool discovery, compact context budgets, and deep IDE integration.

items.label: Claude Code
items.detail: Anthropic's terminal-based agent harness with autonomous multi-turn problem-solving capabilities.

axes.footer_text: Testing across multiple harnesses isolates model intelligence from agent runtime orchestration, measuring how execution environments influence success.

axes.heading: Axis 4: SDK Release Channels
axes.overview: Evaluations run against both Flutter release channels to verify developer-ready reliability and detect framework regressions early.

items.label: Stable
items.detail: The current production SDK release — measures developer-ready reliability on the version used by most teams.

items.label: Beta
items.detail: Monthly beta releases — catches deprecation migrations, API evolutions, and analyzer changes before stable rollout.

axes.footer_text: Ensures AI tooling and skills maintain precision as the Flutter framework and Dart language evolve.

dimensions.title: 1. Outcome
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether the generated code compiles, runs, and fulfills all functional UI and task requirements correctly.

dimensions.title: 2. Code Quality
dimensions.description: Measures code maintainability, static analysis lints, architectural health, and idiomatic Dart 3 standards.

dimensions.title: 3. Developer Experience
dimensions.description: Tracks agent execution friction, tool call accuracy, error recovery loops, and step efficiency.

grader_matrix.title: Grader Matrix
grader_matrix.description: Explore deterministic, LLM-as-a-judge, and heuristic evaluation graders.

graders.name: Build & Run
graders.description: Binary pass/fail checking if code compiles and launches cleanly.

graders.name: Unit & Widget Testing
graders.description: Executes test suites and scores passing test ratio across affected code.

graders.name: Visual Validation
graders.description: Compares DevTools screenshot captures against visual UI expectations.

graders.name: Task Heuristics
graders.description: Task-specific checks verifying dependency additions, required config, and files.

graders.name: Static Analysis
graders.description: Runs `dart analyze` enforcing strict project lint rules.

graders.name: Dart Code Metrics (DCM)
graders.description: Detects dead code, widget complexity, undisposed controllers, and memory leaks.

graders.name: Idiomatic Dart Review
graders.description: Evaluates modern Dart 3 pattern compliance and adherence to Effective Dart.

graders.name: Structural Validation
graders.description: Verifies directory structure, naming conventions, and required file placement.

graders.name: Tool Usage Analysis
graders.description: Checks whether appropriate MCP tools and CLI utilities were called effectively.

graders.name: Step & Token Economy
graders.description: Measures trajectory length, token burn, and redundant execution steps.

graders.name: Error Recovery
graders.description: Rates how fluidly the agent adapts to compiler, analysis, and test errors.

score_triage.title: Score Triage & Action Matrix
score_triage.description: Select a score range to view its criteria and immediate engineering triage actions.

tiers.name: Perfect Success
tiers.heading: Score 1.00 — Perfect Success
tiers.criteria: Code compiles, runs, and passes all unit and widget tests. Zero analyzer or DCM warnings. Idiomatic Dart 3 and flawless DX.

actions.label: Telemetry check
actions.detail: Validate whether all expected tools were utilized.

actions.label: Skip optimization
actions.detail: If expected tools were skipped successfully, re-evaluate if the tool is redundant.

actions.label: Token burn review
actions.detail: If token consumption was high, optimize prompt context and create fast-path shortcut tools.

tiers.name: Minor Flaws
tiers.heading: Score 0.75 – 0.99 — Minor Flaws
tiers.criteria: Code works and functional tests pass, but exhibits minor lint warnings, slightly unidiomatic patterns, or minor DX friction.

actions.label: Prompt tuning
actions.detail: Tune skill prompt instructions for better Dart 3 style enforcement.

actions.label: Schema refinement
actions.detail: Refine tool parameter schemas and validation logic to prevent minor parameter retry hiccups.

actions.label: Model collaboration
actions.detail: Collaborate with model team to polish code generation formatting.

tiers.name: Partial Success
tiers.heading: Score 0.50 – 0.74 — Partial Success
tiers.criteria: Core requirements work but some widget or unit tests fail, lint warnings are significant, or the agent entered noticeable recovery loops.

actions.label: Context gap analysis
actions.detail: Analyze whether the agent lacked key framework or package context.

actions.label: Diagnostic feedback
actions.detail: Refine compiler diagnostic feedback to help the agent self-correct faster.

tiers.name: Poor Implementation
tiers.heading: Score 0.25 – 0.49 — Poor Implementation
tiers.criteria: Fails to compile, ignores constraints, or encountered severe developer experience breakdown during execution.

actions.label: Tool discoverability
actions.detail: If expected tools were ignored, fix tool discoverability, frontmatter, and prompt instructions.

actions.label: Tool output clarity
actions.detail: If tools were used but failed, improve helper tool output clarity and error messaging.

actions.label: Loop prevention
actions.detail: If token burn was high due to endless fix loops, improve compiler errors for single-step healing.

tiers.name: Total Failure
tiers.heading: Score 0.00 — Total Failure
tiers.criteria: No working code produced, severe runtime crash, or agent caught in an infinite loop.

actions.label: Human root-cause audit
actions.detail: Engineers inspect reasoning traces, plan adherence, and test harness logs.

actions.label: Behavior categorization
actions.detail: Identify premature surrender versus infinite loop traps.

actions.label: Constraint refinement
actions.detail: Update benchmark task prompt constraints and bounding parameters.
